title: Scene list
description: Timeline document consumed by the Remotion compositions. All times are in SECONDS (not frames). Scene 1 must start at 0 and every scene must begin exactly where the previous one ends, so the sequence has no gaps or overlaps. Locked to the Mighty Monk formula measured on six films: default scene 3-6 s, news cards 6-45 s, end card 6-20 s, and hard cuts only.
$comment: Duration policy (measured, data in scenes/mighty-monk-master-analysis.json): footage / date scenes 3-6 s, still_card 6-45 s, end_card 6-20 s. Transitions are hard cuts only - the six reference films contained one fade in 1,643 shots, so fade is not offered at all.

id.description: Stable, unique scene number. Also used as the scene's NAME.

end.description: End time in seconds, exclusive. Must be greater than start.

duration.description: Length in seconds. Must equal end - start; src/scenes.ts rejects the file when it does not. Default 3-6 s for footage and date scenes; still_card holds 6-45 s; end_card holds 6-20 s.

footage_query.description: Search term used to find the footage on NASA / Wikimedia Commons / Internet Archive. For still_card it describes the news card instead.

source_preference.description: Preferred archive. A fallback source is allowed at fetch time.

animation_type.description: Which Remotion component renders this scene. ken_burns_zoom / text_overlay / timeline_bar are footage scenes; still_card is a news-article screenshot held on black; date_label is the big white date card; end_card is the channel card that closes the film.

text_overlay.description: On-screen text. For date_label this is the date itself ('18'TH MAY 1974'). For end_card it is the channel line. null means the scene shows no text.

card_image.description: Resolved image for a still_card scene (news screenshot or newspaper page). null for every other animation_type.

sfx_cue.description: Sound-effect cue name resolved against the audio library. null means silent.

transition_in.description: How this scene enters. Only 'cut' exists: the reference films use hard cuts almost exclusively, so no fade or dissolve option is offered.
